report.headline: Strong visual and body response drives well-above-typical engagement through a playful celebrity skincare parody
report.summary: This CeraVe ad performs clearly above 0 for most of its 31 seconds, with the see group — particularly bodies and faces — doing the heavy lifting throughout. The hear group opens strongly then fades as the visual storytelling takes over, while the understand group stays modest but steady. The ad peaks during the spa and massage sequence around seconds 8–14, where bodies and visual responses reach their highest levels. The opening lands well above 0 immediately, helped by strong sound and a recognisable face to camera. Engagement trends downward after second 12 as the scenarios shift to a boardroom setting with smaller faces and less dynamic movement. The final product card at seconds 27–30 shows the expected end drop as faces and bodies leave the frame entirely. The strongest opportunity is the boardroom section around seconds 19–22, which is the weakest stretch of the main video but still sits above 0, and could benefit from tighter cuts or closer faces.

moments.what_happens: Close-up of Michael Cera speaking directly to camera, introducing himself and holding up the CeraVe tub
moments.brain_response: Overall starts at +0.13 and holds there — well above 0. Sound and speech are the lead drivers early on, with the see group building steadily as the face fills the frame.
moments.suggestion: The opening is strong. The direct-to-camera face and immediate speech work together well; no change needed here.

moments.what_happens: Cut to cinematic spa shots: hands massaging a back in a white tent landscape, then two faces reacting at a massage table, then a climber on a rock face
moments.brain_response: This is the video's peak. Overall rises to +0.25 at second 7 and holds near that level through second 14. The bodies signal reaches its highest values (+0.83–0.86) around seconds 8–10, and the see group peaks at +0.50 around seconds 12–14. Sound has faded; pictures fully carry the engagement.
moments.suggestion: The body and scene imagery here is doing exceptional work. If you have any additional cinematic footage of this quality, it would sustain this peak even longer.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera flanked by two other men in open shirts, all holding CeraVe tubs, styled like a fragrance ad
moments.brain_response: Overall holds around +0.17–0.20, still above 0 but noticeably lower than the peak. The see group is declining from its high. Three faces in frame keep engagement from dropping faster.
moments.suggestion: The three-face composition helps. A slightly tighter crop on the trio could lift the faces signal further and slow the decline.

moments.what_happens: Wide boardroom scene: many people seated around a table watching a screen, on-screen text reads CERAVE OFFICES / DERMATOLOGIST REVIEW
moments.brain_response: This is the weakest stretch of the main video. Overall falls to +0.12–0.14. The see group drops as faces become small in the wide shot. Sound reaches nearly 0. The understand group is the only signal holding steadily, around +0.08–0.11.
moments.suggestion: This is the clearest opportunity in the ad. Cutting to closer shots of faces reacting at the table — or intercutting with what is on the boardroom screen — would lift the visual and faces response during this explanation beat.

moments.what_happens: Static product shot: CeraVe tub beside on-screen text reading DEVELOPED WITH DERMATOLOGISTS. NOT MICHAEL CERA.
moments.brain_response: Overall is at -0.04 to -0.06, dipping below 0 as the product card holds static with no people. This is the expected end-card drop.

strengths: The see group — especially bodies and faces — drives engagement well above 0 for the majority of the video, making the visual storytelling the clear strength.

The cinematic spa and massage sequence (seconds 7–14) generates the highest body and visual brain response in the ad, showing that high-production scenic imagery with human movement is very effective here.
The opening is strong from the first second, with sound and speech above 0 immediately and the faces response building quickly — there is no slow or below-0 start.
The three-person styled shot at seconds 16–18 uses multiple faces to slow the natural decline after the peak, keeping overall above 0 through that transition.
improvements: The boardroom wide shots at seconds 19–22 are the weakest stretch of the main video; cutting to closer faces or reaction shots during this section would raise the visual and faces response.

The sound and speech signals fade quickly after the opening, contributing little from second 9 onward; stronger audio design or more vocal delivery in the middle section could add another layer of engagement.
The transition from the cinematic spa peak into the boardroom scene is abrupt and the overall level drops noticeably; a brief bridging shot with a closer face could smooth the fall.
The product card ending holds for about three seconds with no people, pushing overall below 0; even a brief final face-to-camera moment before the card would delay that drop.

report.headline: Strong above-typical engagement driven by faces, bodies and sound — with a genuinely funny, well-crafted opener
report.summary: This CeraVe ad predicts above-typical brain engagement for the majority of its 77 seconds. The see group (faces and bodies in particular) carries the video throughout, while the hear group adds a strong second layer from seconds 8 to 21. The understand group (speech and social) contributes meaningfully from seconds 10 to 25 and again from 54 to 70. Overall stays above 0 from second 8 through to the logo card at second 73, which is a solid result. The opening 7 seconds begin below 0 — dark curtains with no face visible — but the response climbs steadily and reaches typical levels by second 7 as a face first appears, so this is a brief and functional build rather than a problem. The bodies signal is the standout single channel, peaking above +0.60 during the spa massage scene at seconds 29–30. The weakest stretch of the main content is the transition around seconds 62–64, where overall briefly touches 0, though it never falls meaningfully below it. The logo card drop from second 73 is expected.

moments.what_happens: Dark curtains open slowly; no face is visible until second 2 when a silhouette appears, and the product jar appears at second 5.
moments.brain_response: Overall is below 0 for the full opening, bottoming at -0.22 at second 0. All groups are negative. The response rises steadily, crossing 0 for see by second 5 as the jar appears.
moments.suggestion: The below-0 opening is the one structural risk. Even a brief flash of the face or a title card before the curtain reveal would help the visual response build faster.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera steps into frame, speaks directly to camera, holds up the CeraVe jar, and delivers the 'I am CeraVe' claim. The word GENEROSITY appears on screen at second 19.
moments.brain_response: This is the highest-engagement stretch of the video. Overall peaks at +0.29 around seconds 18–19. Sound rises sharply to +0.50 at second 10 as speech begins, and speech itself reaches +0.39 at second 21. The see group holds steadily above +0.20. Overall is clearly above muted_overall throughout, confirming sound and speech drive the lift here.

moments.what_happens: Cut to a luxury spa tent on white sands; a masseur applies cream to a man lying on a table, with the CeraVe jar visible on a side stand.
moments.brain_response: Bodies peaks at its highest point in the video here, reaching +0.63 at second 30. Overall holds around +0.17–+0.21. Sound has dropped close to 0 and speech is quiet, so the pictures carry this stretch entirely — overall and muted_overall are nearly identical.
moments.suggestion: This visually sumptuous scene drives the bodies response to its peak but overall sits only moderately above 0 because sound and speech are low. A line of dialogue or music swell here could lift the full engagement level.

moments.what_happens: Multiple versions of Michael Cera face him in a mirrored room; then the word SKIN appears over curtain imagery; then a CGI narwhal rises from water with the subtitle 'Your skin looks so moisturized, Michael Cera.'
moments.brain_response: Overall softens to its weakest sustained stretch of the main content, ranging from +0.04 to +0.15. Scenes rise to +0.26–+0.27 as the fantastical environments appear, but faces and bodies fall and speech goes negative. Overall and muted_overall converge, meaning sound adds little here.
moments.suggestion: This is the weakest passage of the video, but it stays above 0. The narwhal gag is the comedic centrepiece; consider giving it a stronger audio punchline — a voice, a sound effect, or a music hit — to bring sound and speech back above 0 at this moment.

moments.what_happens: A split-screen of three versions of Michael Cera's face appears simultaneously.
moments.brain_response: Overall holds around +0.08–+0.10, with faces the dominant signal at +0.16. Bodies drops below 0 as the body-less close-ups fill the frame. Sound holds around +0.18–+0.20 and speech around +0.20–+0.23, so the hear and understand groups are carrying this shot more than the see group.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera stands flanked by two tall, open-shirted men holding CeraVe jars, in a slow, posed hero shot.
moments.brain_response: Overall is at +0.04–+0.09, above 0 but the lowest of the second half. Bodies is negative (-0.12 to -0.22), faces is only weakly positive, and speech is at +0.08–+0.18. Overall and muted_overall are close, meaning pictures and sound contribute roughly equally at this low level.
moments.suggestion: The hero product shot with flanking figures reads as a visual pay-off but the brain data suggests it lands softly. Bringing the camera closer to faces rather than holding a wide group pose could lift the faces and bodies response for this final impression before the logo.

strengths: The core Michael Cera performance segment (seconds 8–25) is the strongest stretch, with sound, speech and faces all above 0 simultaneously — a rare combination that suggests high attention.
The bodies response is the single highest-value channel in the video, peaking above +0.60 during the spa scene, showing the production design and physical comedy land well.
Overall stays above 0 for roughly 65 consecutive seconds once it rises, indicating sustained above-typical engagement across the bulk of the ad.
The sound-to-muted gap is clearly positive in the first half, confirming the spoken comedy and music work together to add engagement beyond what the pictures alone achieve.
improvements: The opening 7 seconds are below 0 across all groups; showing a face or title card earlier would help the response build before the joke lands.

The narwhal / fantastical sequence (seconds 44–51) is the weakest passage; adding a stronger audio moment — voice, music hit or sound effect — could recover the hear and understand groups at the comedic peak.
The spa scene (seconds 27–33) has a high bodies response but low sound and speech; a line of dialogue or music lift would raise overall engagement to match the visual quality.
The final group hero shot (seconds 67–70) lands softly just before the logo; a tighter frame on faces rather than a wide posed tableau could sustain the faces signal through to the end.

report.headline: B opens stronger; A sustains longer with richer visuals — two cuts of one CeraVe campaign
report.summary: These are two cuts of the same Michael Cera CeraVe campaign. B opens immediately above 0 with a face and speech, reaching stronger see and bodies peaks (0.46–0.86) mid-video. A spends its first 6 seconds below 0 behind curtains before rising. A compensates with a longer, richer middle act — spa, rock climbing, fantasy scenes — sustaining overall above 0 for roughly 60 seconds. Both end with expected logo-card drops.

differences.what_differs: A opens on dark curtains with no face, starting with faces and overall well below 0; B opens immediately on Michael Cera's face with speech already running, faces above 0 from the first second and overall at +0.13.
differences.brain_response: B's opening draws stronger face, body and sound engagement from second 0, while A's response stays negative until about second 7 as the silhouette slowly emerges.

differences.what_differs: Both videos share the spa massage scene and rock-climbing sequence; in A these run from about 27–41 s with bodies peaking at +0.65, while in B the same material is compressed into 7–14 s with bodies peaking at +0.86 and faces at +0.55.
differences.brain_response: B's version of this shared material produces noticeably higher bodies and faces signals, likely because B reaches it while sound and prior face engagement are still elevated, whereas A arrives there after speech has faded.

differences.what_differs: A contains an extended sequence of Michael Cera holding the CeraVe jar with on-screen text 'GENEROSITY' and direct-to-camera delivery, with sound peaking at +0.46 and speech at +0.39 around 19–21 s — material absent from B.
differences.brain_response: This stretch gives A its highest hear and speech values in the entire video, lifting overall to +0.29 and showing that sound and speech carry this section well above what pictures alone would achieve.

a_does_better: A sustains overall engagement above 0 for roughly 60 continuous seconds versus B's 22, giving the longer creative arc more time with the audience above typical viewing levels.
A's extended fantasy and multi-face sequences (48–70 s) keep faces and scenes above 0 through the back half, while B has already wound down by that point.
b_does_better: B's opening is above 0 immediately with a recognisable face and speech from second 0, avoiding the below-zero warm-up that costs A its first six seconds.
B reaches its highest bodies and faces values (+0.86, +0.55) earlier and at greater magnitude than A's peak for the same shared material, suggesting tighter pacing amplifies the visual response.
suggestions: Consider starting A with a direct face shot — even one second of Michael Cera before the curtain reveal — to avoid the below-zero opening that B sidesteps entirely.

The 'GENEROSITY' speech sequence in A (19–21 s) produces the video's highest sound and speech scores; a version of this high-engagement moment is missing from B and could be worth adding or signalling more clearly there.
